@@ -0,0 +1,180 @@
+---
+title: Configure Secure Cloud User Integration for single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID
+description: Learn how to configure single sign-on (SSO) between Microsoft Entra ID and Secure Cloud User Integration using OpenID Connect (OIDC).
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 10/23/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an IT administrator, I want to configure single sign-on between Microsoft Entra ID and Secure Cloud User Integration so that users can sign in with their Microsoft Entra accounts and I can centrally manage access.
+---
+
+# Configure Secure Cloud User Integration for single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID
+
+In this article, you learn how to configure single sign-on (SSO) between Microsoft Entra ID and Secure Cloud using OpenID Connect (OIDC). When you integrate Secure Cloud with Microsoft Entra ID, users can sign in with their Microsoft Entra accounts, and administrators can centrally manage access.
+
+The **Secure Cloud User Integration** enterprise application is created in your Microsoft Entra tenant during the initial Microsoft Entra sign-in and consent process.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin, ensure that you have the following prerequisites:
+
+- [A Microsoft Entra tenant](~/identity-platform/quickstart-create-new-tenant.md).
+- A Microsoft Entra account with one of the following roles or ownership permissions:
+    - [Application Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#application-administrator).
+    - [Cloud Application Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#cloud-application-administrator).
+    - [Application owner](~/fundamentals/users-default-permissions.md#owned-enterprise-applications).
+- An account authorized to grant the required application consent in your tenant. The ability to manage an application doesn't by itself determine whether you can grant consent. For more information, see [Overview of user and admin consent](~/identity/enterprise-apps/user-admin-consent-overview.md).
+- A [Secure Cloud](https://cp.appriver.com/) administrator account.
+- A Secure Cloud user account whose email address matches the Microsoft Entra account that you use for the initial setup.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Secure Cloud User Integration uses consent-based onboarding. The enterprise application doesn't exist in your tenant until an administrator completes the initial Microsoft Entra sign-in and grants consent. Follow the setup steps in order before looking for the application in Microsoft Entra ID.
+
+## Scenario description
+
+In this article, you enable Microsoft Entra authentication in Secure Cloud, sign in with Microsoft Entra credentials, grant consent, and verify SSO.
+
+- Secure Cloud supports service provider (SP)-initiated and identity provider (IdP)-initiated SSO.
+- Secure Cloud uses OpenID Connect (OIDC) for Microsoft Entra ID authentication.
+- Secure Cloud also supports automatic user provisioning.
+
+## Step 1: Enable Microsoft Entra authentication
+
+Configure authentication in Secure Cloud before you initiate the first Microsoft Entra sign-in.
+
+1. Sign in to [Secure Cloud](https://cp.appriver.com/) as an administrator.
+1. Browse to **Service Administration** > **Account Management** > **User Integration** > **Authentication**.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the User Integration page with Authentication highlighted.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/navigate-authentication.png)
+
+1. In the **Authentication Type** list, select **Microsoft Entra SSO**.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Authentication Type list with Microsoft Entra SSO highlighted.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/select-authentication-type.png)
+
+1. Under **Configuration**, turn on **Enable Microsoft Entra Authentication**.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Configuration section with Enable Microsoft Entra Authentication turned on.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/enable-microsoft-entra-authentication.png)
+
+1. Optionally, enable **Fallback User Password** during initial setup. This option provides an alternate sign-in method if Microsoft Entra authentication is unavailable.
+
+    - If **Fallback User Password** is enabled, users can select **Sign in with Microsoft**, or sign in with their Secure Cloud credentials or LDAP credentials, if LDAP authentication is configured.
+    - If **Fallback User Password** is disabled, users are redirected to Microsoft Entra ID after entering their username. Secure Cloud credentials and LDAP credentials aren't available as alternate sign-in methods.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Microsoft Entra SSO Settings section with Fallback User Password enabled.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/fallback-user-password.png)
+
+1. Select **Save**.
+
+## Step 2: Initiate Microsoft Entra sign-in
+
+Start the sign-in flow from Secure Cloud.
+
+1. Sign out of Secure Cloud, or use a different browser, and go to the [Secure Cloud sign-in page](https://account.appriver.com/).
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Secure Cloud sign-in page.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/secure-cloud-sign-in.png)
+
+1. Enter the username of a Secure Cloud account whose email address matches a Microsoft Entra account authorized to grant consent in your tenant, and then select **Continue**.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Secure Cloud sign-in page with Continue highlighted.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/secure-cloud-sign-in-continue.png)
+
+1. Continue according to your **Fallback User Password** setting:
+
+    - If it's disabled, you're redirected to Microsoft Entra ID automatically.
+    - If it's enabled, select **Sign in with Microsoft** under **Use your organization's digital identity**.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Secure Cloud sign-in page with Sign in with Microsoft highlighted.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/secure-cloud-sign-in-with-microsoft.png)
+
+## Step 3: Authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID
+
+Secure Cloud redirects you to the Microsoft identity platform sign-in experience.
+
+1. Enter your Microsoft Entra credentials.
+1. Complete any required multifactor authentication prompts.
+1. Continue to the consent screen.
+
+If consent has already been granted, you might be signed in without another consent prompt. In that case, continue to [Step 5](#step-5-complete-sign-in).
+
+## Step 4: Grant consent to the application
+
+If consent hasn't already been granted, the **Permissions requested** page appears.
+
+1. Review the requested permissions.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Permissions requested page.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/secure-cloud-user-integration-permissions-requested.png)
+
+1. Optionally, select **Consent on behalf of your organization** if you're authorized to grant tenant-wide admin consent. This grants consent for users in the tenant so that they aren't prompted to grant the same consent individually.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Permissions requested page with Consent on behalf of your organization selected.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/secure-cloud-user-integration-permissions-requested-organization-consent.png)
+
+1. Select **Accept**.
+
+After consent is granted, Microsoft Entra ID creates the **Secure Cloud User Integration** enterprise application in your tenant.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> If organizational consent isn't granted, users might be prompted to consent individually during their first sign-in, depending on your tenant's consent policies.
+
+For more information, see [Consent experience for applications in Microsoft Entra ID](~/identity-platform/application-consent-experience.md) and [Overview of user and admin consent](~/identity/enterprise-apps/user-admin-consent-overview.md).
+
+## Step 5: Complete sign-in
+
+After consent is granted, Microsoft Entra ID redirects you back to Secure Cloud. Secure Cloud validates the authentication response and signs you in with your Microsoft Entra account.
+
+The enterprise application created during consent is used for subsequent SSO and provisioning configuration.
+
+## Step 6: Verify enterprise application creation
+
+Confirm that the initial sign-in and consent process created the application.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Cloud Application Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#cloud-application-administrator).
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Enterprise apps**.
+1. Search for **Secure Cloud User Integration** and confirm that the application appears in the list.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the Enterprise applications list with Secure Cloud User Integration highlighted.](./media/secure-cloud-user-integration-tutorial/secure-cloud-user-integration-listed.png)
+
+## Test single sign-on
+
+Verify that you can sign in to Secure Cloud with your Microsoft Entra account.
+
+1. Sign out of Secure Cloud.
+1. Return to [Secure Cloud](https://cp.appriver.com/).
+1. Enter the username of the Secure Cloud account that matches your Microsoft Entra account, and then select **Continue**.
+1. If **Fallback User Password** is enabled, select **Sign in with Microsoft** under **Use your organization's digital identity**. If it's disabled, you're redirected to Microsoft Entra ID automatically.
+1. Authenticate with your Microsoft Entra account.
+
+If authentication succeeds, you're redirected to the Secure Cloud portal and signed in without being prompted for a Secure Cloud password.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+Use the following checks if application creation, consent, or sign-in doesn't complete as expected.
+
+### The enterprise application doesn't appear
+
+The application is created only after an administrator completes the initial Microsoft Entra sign-in and consent process.
+
+- Verify that the Microsoft Entra sign-in process completed successfully.
+- Verify that you selected **Accept** on the consent page.
+- Verify that your browser redirected you back to Secure Cloud.
+- If needed, repeat the [initial sign-in](#step-2-initiate-microsoft-entra-sign-in) and consent process.
+
+### Users can't grant consent
+
+If users see a message that administrator approval is required:
+
+- Check the tenant's consent settings.
+- Contact a Microsoft Entra administrator authorized to grant the required consent.
+- Have an authorized administrator review the requested permissions and grant consent on behalf of the organization.
+
+For more information, see [Overview of user and admin consent](~/identity/enterprise-apps/user-admin-consent-overview.md).
+
+### A user can't sign in
+
+Verify the following settings:
+
+- The user exists in Secure Cloud.
+- The Secure Cloud user's email address matches the Microsoft Entra account.
+- **Enable Microsoft Entra Authentication** is turned on in Secure Cloud.
+- The sign-in path matches the configured **Fallback User Password** setting.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Consent experience for applications in Microsoft Entra ID](~/identity-platform/application-consent-experience.md).
+- [Overview of user and admin consent](~/identity/enterprise-apps/user-admin-consent-overview.md).
+- [Automate user provisioning and deprovisioning to SaaS applications with Microsoft Entra ID](~/identity/app-provisioning/user-provisioning.md).

+---

+

+---
+# What are Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plans? (preview)
+
+Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plans group related rules under shared assignments and conditions. Administrators can define common targeting and exclusions once, then configure each rule for a specific scenario. Use a plan to organize related controls around a security objective, such as requiring compliant devices or securing agent activity.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Conditional Access policy plans are in preview. Preview features are available under the [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) and might not have all the capabilities of generally available features.
+
+## Why use policy plans?
+
+### Reduce policy sprawl
+
+An organization might maintain separate Conditional Access policies for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android when each platform requires different settings. Those policies can repeat the same user targeting and emergency access exclusions. Changes to that shared targeting must then be made in each policy.
+
+With a plan, shared targeting is defined once and automatically applies to every scenario within that plan. Adding or removing an emergency access group in one place updates the shared targeting for all rules in the plan.
+
+### Eliminate duplicated exclusions
+
+Emergency access accounts, trusted service accounts, and privileged workstations appear in exclusion lists across many policies. Missed exclusions are a common source of unintended lockouts. Plans let administrators define these exclusions once, at the plan level, so no individual rule can accidentally omit them.
+
+### Scale for Global Secure Access
+
+Organizations that deploy Global Secure Access often need hundreds of network-scoped rules that target the same user population and application set. Plans allow the shared targeting to be defined once, with each rule focused only on the specific network scope it governs.
+
+### Apply consistent controls to agent activity
+
+Agent identities can act with their own permissions or on behalf of a user by using the user's permissions. A plan can define a shared condition, such as high agent risk, and use separate rules to protect agent users and autonomous agents. Without a plan, each scenario requires a standalone policy that repeats the shared condition.
+
+## How plans work
+
+A plan has three parts:
+
+- **Plan details**: Specify a name, description, optional tags, and individual or group owners. These details help teams understand the plan's purpose, accountability, and the potential impact of future changes. Designating owners doesn't affect who has permission to edit the plan, and plan details don't affect policy enforcement at runtime.
+- **Shared conditions**: Define optional include and exclude targeting that applies broadly. Shared conditions can include identities; resources such as applications; user actions; authentication context; risk levels; device platforms; network locations; and client app types.
+- **Rules**: Define the individual enforcement scenarios within the plan. Each rule adds the assignments and conditions that are specific to the scenario, along with its grant and session controls. Every policy plan must have at least one rule.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Select **All resources** at the rule level. This assignment isn't available in shared conditions.
+
+### How shared conditions affect rules
+
+Shared conditions and rule conditions combine additively:
+
+- **Targeting at the plan level is inherited.** If the plan targets group A, every rule in the plan inherits that scope. A rule can't narrow the plan's targeting, but it can add exclusions of its own. For this reason, you can target **All users** in rules but not in shared conditions.
+- **Identity type must be consistent.** Shared conditions can't mix identity types. A plan that targets users can't also target agents at the plan level. To cover multiple identity types in one plan, leave the identity assignment to the rules. For example, one rule can target users and another can target agents.
+- **Inclusions and exclusions accumulate.** If the plan excludes emergency access groups A and B, and a rule also excludes group C, the effective exclusion list is A, B, and C. An exclusion set at the plan level can never be overridden or removed by a rule. This design ensures consistency across every rule in the plan.
+
+## Runtime enforcement
+
+At sign-in time, Conditional Access combines a rule's conditions with the plan's shared conditions, if any, to form the complete targeting for that rule. Each rule is then evaluated as an independent enforcement decision in the same way as a standalone policy. Each rule appears separately in sign-in logs.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> During preview, policy plans that target users with Location as a condition will be issued one-hour access tokens without instant IP enforcement check. For more information, see [Named location limitations](concept-continuous-access-evaluation.md#named-location-limitations).
+
+## Relationship to existing Conditional Access policies
+
+Plans are an addition to the existing Conditional Access policy model, not a replacement. Your existing policies continue to work as they do today, with no changes required.
+
+During sign-in evaluation, the Conditional Access engine evaluates both existing policies and policy plan rules. Every applicable policy and every applicable rule must be satisfied for access to be granted. There's no interaction or precedence between them. They accumulate independently.
+
+| Capability | Existing policy | Policy plans and rules |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Targeting | Defined per policy and duplicated across policies | Shared conditions are defined once at the plan level and inherited by all rules, or defined per rule |
+| Change management | Each policy is updated individually | A single change to the plan's shared conditions propagates to all rules |
+| Policy templates | One template per policy | Combine multiple templates into a single plan, or deploy one template per plan |
+
+## Required roles
+
+To create, modify, or delete a policy plan, sign in with the Conditional Access Administrator role.
+
+## License requirements
+
+For license requirements, see [Conditional Access license requirements](overview.md#license-requirements).
+
+## Next steps
+
+- [Create a Conditional Access policy plan](how-to-create-conditional-access-policy-plan.md)
+- [Migrate Conditional Access policies to a policy plan](how-to-migrate-conditional-access-policy-plan.md)

+---
+title: Create a Conditional Access policy plan (preview)
+description: Learn how to create a Conditional Access policy plan from a template or from scratch in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
+
+ms.service: entra-id
+ms.subservice: conditional-access

+
+ms.author: etbasser
+author: ebasseri

+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+#customer intent: As a Conditional Access administrator, I want to create a policy plan so that I can manage shared targeting and exclusions across related rules.
+---
+# Create a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy plan (preview)
+
+This article shows you how to create a Conditional Access policy plan in the Microsoft Entra admin center, either from a built-in template or from scratch. For background on how plans work and why to use them, see [What are Conditional Access policy plans?](concept-conditional-access-policy-plans.md).
+
+Before you create a plan, identify its security objective. For example, a plan might protect employees at a specific location, secure agent activity, or require compliant devices. Add only the assignments and conditions that apply to every scenario to the plan's shared conditions. Configure variations of the objective as individual rules.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Conditional Access policy plans are in preview. Preview features are available under the [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) and might not have all the capabilities of generally available features.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+To create, modify, or delete a policy plan, sign in with the Conditional Access Administrator role.
+
+For license requirements, see [Conditional Access license requirements](overview.md#license-requirements).
+
+Before you begin, read [What are Conditional Access policy plans?](concept-conditional-access-policy-plans.md) to understand how shared conditions and rules interact.
+
+## User exclusions
+
+Conditional Access policies are powerful tools. We recommend excluding the following accounts from your policies:
+
+- **Emergency access** accounts to prevent lockout because of policy misconfiguration. In the unlikely scenario where all administrators are locked out, your emergency access administrative account can be used to sign in and recover access. For more information, see [Manage emergency access accounts in Microsoft Entra ID](../role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md).
+- **Service accounts** and **service principals**, such as the Microsoft Entra Connect Sync Account. Service accounts are noninteractive accounts that aren't tied to a specific user. They're typically used by back-end services to allow programmatic access to applications. Calls made by service principals aren't blocked by Conditional Access policies scoped to users. Use [Conditional Access for workload identities](workload-identity.md) to define policies that target service principals.
+
+> [!TIP]
+> With policy plans, add emergency access accounts and service accounts to the plan's **shared conditions** exclusion list instead of repeating them in each rule. Exclusions set at the plan level apply to every rule automatically and can't be removed by an individual rule.
+
+## Create a policy plan from a template
+
+Templates provide preconfigured shared conditions and rules for common Conditional Access scenarios, including plans that secure agent activity. Starting from a template creates the plan, shared conditions, and one or more rules in a single flow.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#conditional-access-administrator).
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policy plans (Preview)**.
+1. Select **Create policy from template**.
+1. Browse the available templates, select **Use template** for one or more templates, and then select **Create plan**.
+1. On the **Create plan from templates** tab, customize the name if needed. Under **Shared conditions**, review any prepopulated targeting, and then select **Create policy plan**. The initial **State** for all rules generated by a template is **Off** to prevent unintended impact to your organization.
+1. After the plan is created, select **Edit plan**. Select **Add Users** > **Exclude** to add your organization's emergency access accounts and any service accounts that must be excluded from every rule in the plan. Modify any other shared conditions as needed.
+1. In the **Rules** list, review the prepopulated rules. Select a rule to edit its name, conditions, or grant controls. Each rule is evaluated independently at sign-in time.
+1. For each rule, change **State** from **Off** to **Report-only**. Report-only mode lets you validate the effect in sign-in logs before enforcement begins.
+
+After you review the effect by using [report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only.md), return to each rule, set **State** to **On**, and save your changes.
+
+## Create a custom policy plan
+
+Build a plan from scratch when your scenario isn't covered by a template, or when you want full control over shared conditions and rules from the start.
+
+### Create the plan
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#conditional-access-administrator).
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policy plans (Preview)**, and then select **Create policy**.
+1. On the **Create policy plan** tab, enter a name. Optionally, add a description and tags. Your account is automatically added as an owner. Add other individual or group owners as needed to record accountability. The owner field is for accountability only and doesn't grant permissions to policy plans.
+
+### Configure shared conditions
+
+Shared conditions are optional and apply to every rule in the plan.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Add only assignments and conditions that apply to every rule to shared conditions. Configure anything that varies by scenario in the individual rules. You can add exclusions at the rule level, but you can't remove or override exclusions set in shared conditions. Identity type must be consistent. A plan that targets users at the plan level can't also target workload identities at the plan level.
+
+1. Under **Add users, agents or workload identities**, select the identities to include or exclude that every rule in the plan should target. **All users** isn't available at the plan level. Exclude emergency access accounts and service accounts in shared conditions so the exclusions propagate to every rule.
+1. Under **Add resources, user actions or authentication context**, optionally scope the plan to include or exclude a shared set of applications, actions, or contexts.
+1. Under **Add condition**, optionally configure shared risk levels, device platforms, network locations, or client app types that should apply across all rules.
+1. Select **Continue** to add your first rule.
+
+### Add rules to the plan
+
+Every plan must have at least one rule. Each rule inherits the plan's shared assignments and conditions, so you don't need to configure them again. The rule adds the assignments, conditions, and controls that are specific to its scenario.
+
+1. Enter a name and optional description for the rule.
+1. Under **State**, select **Report-only**.
+1. Under **Add users, agents or workload identities**, select the identities to include or exclude.
+1. Under **Add resources, user actions or authentication context**, scope the rule to include or exclude applications, actions, or contexts. Select **All resources** here when the rule should protect every resource.
+1. Under **Add condition**, include conditions that should apply, or exclude specific device platforms, networks, or locations. These conditions combine with the plan's shared conditions at evaluation time.
+1. Under **Add control** > **Grant**, select the grant controls to enforce when the rule matches.
+1. Under **Add control** > **Session**, optionally configure session controls.
+1. Review the plan and its initial rule, and then select **Create**.
+1. Repeat these steps for each additional scenario. Each rule appears as an independent entry in sign-in logs.
+
+After you review the impact with the built-in policy impact metrics or in sign-in logs by using [report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only.md), return to each rule, set **State** to **On**, and save your changes.
+
+## Next steps
+
+- [What are Conditional Access policy plans?](concept-conditional-access-policy-plans.md)
+- [Migrate Conditional Access policies to a policy plan](how-to-migrate-conditional-access-policy-plan.md)
+- [Analyze Conditional Access policy impact](concept-conditional-access-report-only.md)

+

+---
+# Migrate Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies to a policy plan (preview)
+
+This article shows you how to consolidate existing Conditional Access policies into a policy plan by using the built-in migration experience. The migration tool analyzes your selected policies, identifies shared conditions, and proposes a plan structure for you to review before committing. Your original policies aren't changed during this process.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Conditional Access policy plans are in preview. Preview features are available under the [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) and might not have all the capabilities of generally available features.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+To migrate Conditional Access policies, sign in with the Conditional Access Administrator role.
+
+For license requirements, see [Conditional Access license requirements](overview.md#license-requirements).
+
+Before you begin, read [What are Conditional Access policy plans?](concept-conditional-access-policy-plans.md) to understand how shared conditions and rules interact, and how plan rules evaluate alongside existing policies.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+The migration experience works best when you select policies that share a common intent. For example, select policies that protect the same set of applications but apply different controls to different user types, risk levels, or device states.
+
+When you plan your migration:
+
+- **Group by protected resource.** Policies that protect the same applications or services are natural candidates for a single plan.
+- **Group by persona.** If multiple policies apply to the same set of users with different grant controls, they can be consolidated into one plan. Shared user targeting lives at the plan level, and each grant control becomes a rule.
+- **Group by condition.** Separate policies that already share a common condition, such as a sign-in risk level, device platform, or network location, are candidates for a plan. Configure the shared condition at the plan level and the scenario-specific settings in each rule.
+- **Migrate incrementally.** You don't need to migrate all policies at once. Starting with a small, well-understood group of related policies reduces risk during validation.
+
+## Migrate policies to a plan
+
+After you identify a related set of policies, use the migration experience to review and create a proposed plan:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#conditional-access-administrator).
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**.
+1. On the **Policies** page, locate the **Migrate to Conditional Access Policy plans (Preview)** banner, and then select **Get started**.
+1. Select the existing policies that you want to consolidate into a single plan. Choose policies that share a common intent. You can search for specific policies or filter on policy attributes.
+1. Select **Merge policies into a plan**.
+1. The migration tool analyzes the selected policies and identifies any **shared conditions**. Update the policy plan name if needed.
+1. Review the plan preview. Settings that the selected policies have in common become **shared conditions**.
+1. Review the proposed **Rules**. Each selected policy is mapped to a rule. Identities, resources, locations, grant controls, session controls, and other settings that are unique to a policy remain in its corresponding rule. Note that the initial **State** for all rules generated during migration is **Off** to prevent unintended impact to your organization.
+1. Select **Create policy plan**. 
+1. Select **Edit plan** to update the plan's name, description, tags, and owners to record accountability and organizational context.
+1. Select a rule to edit its details as needed.
+1. Update each rule's **State** to **Report-only** when you are ready.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Your original policies aren't changed by the migration. They remain in their previous state, whether on, off, or report-only, and continue to evaluate independently. Original policies that are set to **On** continue to enforce access. New plan rules that are set to **Report-only** record their results in sign-in logs without enforcing controls.
+
+## Validate the plan
+
+After you configure the rules to **Report-only**, use the built-in policy impact metrics or sign-in logs to confirm that the rules produce the expected results before you enable enforcement.
+
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**.
+1. Review sign-in events to confirm that each rule in the plan matches the expected users, applications, and conditions.
+1. Compare the plan rule behavior against the original policy behavior. The results should be equivalent.
+1. When you're satisfied with the results, return to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policy plans (Preview)**, open the plan, and set each rule's **State** to **On**.
+
+For more information about validating policy behavior before enforcement, see [Analyze Conditional Access policy impact](concept-conditional-access-report-only.md).
+
+## Decommission the original policies
+
+After you enable and validate the plan rules, disable the original policies. Delete them only after the validation period and when your organization's change-management and retention requirements allow it.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> During sign-in evaluation, existing policies and policy plan rules evaluate independently. Every applicable policy and every applicable rule must be satisfied for access to be granted. Disable the original policies only after you're confident that the plan covers your intended security posture.
+
+1. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**.
+1. For each policy that was migrated to the plan, open the policy and set its state to **Off**.
+1. Confirm that sign-in behavior remains consistent after the original policies are disabled.
+1. After the validation period, delete the original policies if your organization's change-management and retention requirements allow it.
+
+## Maintain the migrated plan
+
+When a new scenario supports the same security objective, add it as a rule in the existing plan instead of creating another standalone policy. Update shared conditions when a change should apply to every rule in the plan.
+
+## Next steps
+
+- [What are Conditional Access policy plans?](concept-conditional-access-policy-plans.md)
+- [Create a Conditional Access policy plan](how-to-create-conditional-access-policy-plan.md)
+- [Analyze Conditional Access policy impact](concept-conditional-access-report-only.md)
